resources.string: New iMessages that arrive through OpenBubbles, with Reply.

Blue Bubbles sends and receives iMessages through the OpenBubbles app, which connects to iMessage with the help of your iPhone. Install OpenBubbles and finish its setup first, then come back and tick Blue Bubbles.
This OpenBubbles is not the real one

An app is installed under OpenBubbles\' name, but it is not signed as OpenBubbles from Google Play, so LightDecoder does not read its notifications, send through it or give it files. Remove it and install OpenBubbles from Google Play.

LightDecoder reads the iMessages OpenBubbles shows in its notifications and replies through them. Turn on notification access for LightDecoder on the next screen.\n\nIf Android says the setting is restricted, open LightDecoder\'s App info, tap ⋮ and choose Allow restricted settings, then try again.

iMessage chats now show here in Messages, marked iMessage, as soon as a message arrives in OpenBubbles. Replies you send from them go out as iMessages.

• Set OpenBubbles' notifications to Silent (not off), or you will be alerted twice.
• In OpenBubbles: Settings → Notifications, turn ON “Send Notifications on Chat List” and turn OFF “Hide Message Text”, so every message reaches LightDecoder.
• A message that arrives while its chat is open in OpenBubbles does not reach LightDecoder (OpenBubbles shows no notification then).
• Earlier messages, and messages you send from OpenBubbles or other devices, do not show here.
• Pictures, and chats nobody has written in since LightDecoder started, open in OpenBubbles for you to tap send.
Blue Bubbles is off. iMessage chats no longer show in Messages.
Tick Blue Bubbles in the Messages menu to show iMessages here.
No iMessage chats yet. They show up as messages arrive in OpenBubbles.
This could not be sent from here. Tap it to finish sending it in OpenBubbles.
Try sending this again through OpenBubbles?

LightDecoder needs notifications to tell you about new iMessages.

LightDecoder will send this to %1$s as an iMessage:

“%2$s”

Ask them to reply. An iPhone replies the way the conversation shows on it: by iMessage when it is blue, by text when it is green. So their reply tells you which colour they see.
iMessage is on, through the iMessage library built into LightDecoder: messages go straight to Apple, and arrive whether LightDecoder is open or not.

Blue Bubbles is on and working: OpenBubbles is installed and LightDecoder is reading its notifications.\n\nSo that every message reaches LightDecoder: in OpenBubbles, Settings → Notifications, turn ON \u201cSend Notifications on Chat List\u201d and OFF \u201cHide Message Text\u201d. A message that arrives while its chat is open in OpenBubbles is not seen here.

OpenBubbles is hiding message text in its notifications (they only say \u201ciMessage\u201d), so LightDecoder cannot show what was said. In OpenBubbles: Settings → Notifications, turn OFF \u201cHide Message Text\u201d.
Blue Bubbles is off: messages go as texts. Turn it on in this menu.
This conversation sends as iMessage (blue), straight through OpenBubbles.
This conversation sends as iMessage (blue), but OpenBubbles opens for you to tap send. It sends straight from here again after their next iMessage.
This conversation sends as texts (green): there is no iMessage chat with this person yet. Use Send iMessage or Check iMessage in this menu to start one.
Group conversations here send as texts (green). Use OpenBubbles for iMessage groups.
OpenBubbles is not installed, so nothing can go as iMessage.
The OpenBubbles installed is not signed as OpenBubbles from Google Play, so LightDecoder does not use it and nothing can go as iMessage.
LightDecoder is not allowed to read notifications, so it cannot see or answer iMessages. Allow it in Android settings (Notification access).
Android has stopped LightDecoder\u2019s notification reader, so new iMessages are missed until it starts again. Turning notification access off and on for LightDecoder restarts it.

OpenBubbles’ notifications only say “Image”, so LightDecoder shows the picture from the copy OpenBubbles saves in your gallery, at full quality.

In OpenBubbles: Settings → Attachments, turn ON “Auto-save Attachments” (and keep Auto-download on).

Pictures that came before that show once you open them in OpenBubbles, if Auto-save is on then.
LightDecoder needs to see your photos and videos to show iMessage pictures. It only looks at the ones OpenBubbles saved.
LightDecoder can only see the photos you picked, so new iMessage pictures cannot show. In Android settings, allow LightDecoder all photos and videos.
In OpenBubbles, long-press the message and tap Edit (Apple allows it for 15 minutes).
In OpenBubbles, double-tap the message and pick %1$s.
Replying to %1$s (sent as an iMessage of its own)
In OpenBubbles, long-press the message and tap Undo Send. Then delete it here too.
Apple only lets an iMessage be unsent within 2 minutes of sending, so it stays on their iPhone. You can still delete it here, on this phone only.
%1$s (same name: link it only if it is this person)
Every iMessage chat is already inside a conversation. A chat shows up here once OpenBubbles has notified about a message in it.
Linked: its iMessages show in this conversation
Its iMessages will show as a conversation of their own instead of here. Messages to this person go as texts (green) until you link it again.
There is no iMessage chat with them in LightDecoder yet: OpenBubbles opens a new one with the check filled in. Tap send there.
OpenBubbles opened its share screen with the message. Pick or start the chat with them there (their number is copied).
OpenBubbles opened. Start a chat with them there: their number is copied, paste it as the recipient.
OpenBubbles is installed but would not open. Open it once by itself, then try again.
No reply from %1$s. The check has ended; a reply that comes later still shows in the conversation (a blue bubble from them means iMessage).
Sent from OpenBubbles (you tap send there)

After tapping send in OpenBubbles, come straight back here, and do not keep that chat open in OpenBubbles: OpenBubbles shows no notification for a reply in a chat that is open on its screen, so LightDecoder would not see it.

Your Apple Account and password go only to Apple. The sign-in is made on this phone by LightDecoder\'s built-in iMessage library; no other company\'s sign-in server is used.
